planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions shallowly in late summer to fall into consistently wet, slightly acidic soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every 3-4 years after bloom.

directions: A Mary Swords DeBaillon Medal winner after earlier Award of Merit and Honorable Mention honors, this modern Louisiana iris carries light yellow standards with a claret streak and feathered edges, claret style arms, and yellow falls washed rusty-red with a serrated claret rim around a yellow-and-green steeple signal. Bred from 'Shining Times' x 'Our Dorothy', it blooms early-to-midseason, extending the Louisiana iris season at the start. Like other Louisiana iris, it performs best where roots never fully dry out.
sources: American Iris Society garden awards records

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in late summer into consistently wet to boggy, fertile soil in full sun; its late bloom extends a Gulf Coast iris bed's display after earlier cultivars finish.

directions: An Award of Merit winner with striking deep wine-purple coloring, this cultivar was bred by Louisiana hybridizer Joe Musacchia and named for the Cajun folklore werewolf-figure. It bears deep wine-purple standards and style arms with white at the base, matching wine-purple falls, and a yellow signal, opening late in the Louisiana iris season. Grow in full sun in consistently wet to boggy, fertile soil, dividing every three to four years in late summer.
sources: American Iris Society garden awards records

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in late summer into reliably wet, slightly acidic soil in full sun; divide every 3-4 years to maintain bloom count.

directions: A modern award-cycle cultivar from respected hybridizer Hooker Nichols, this Louisiana iris carries vivid medium red-rose standards with a cream-white underwash and deeper red-rose veining, yellow-red-rose style arms, and lightly ruffled red falls with a gold signal. Bred from 'Chuck Begnaud' x 'Jacaranda Lad' on a tall, well-branched stalk, it blooms midseason to late. Give it full sun and reliably wet, slightly acidic soil.
sources: Garden Club of Houston plant database

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in late summer into consistently moist to wet soil in full sun; its early bloom pairs well with later cultivars to extend the season.

directions: An Award of Merit winner with a bright yellow-and-red bitone pattern, this cultivar was bred by Florida hybridizer Harry Wolford from 'Splitter Splatter' x 'Bayou Tiger' and released through Louisiana Iris Gardens. It opens early in the bloom season with bright yellow standards and falls heavily veined in red and bright red style arms edged yellow. Plant in full sun in consistently moist to wet soil, dividing crowded clumps every three to four years after bloom.
sources: Garden Club of Houston plant database
